children: will post fiscal first-quarter results on Thursday after the market close, with analysts expecting earnings of $1.74 per share on revenue of $19.13B, representing year-over-year growth of 18.4% and 28.2%, respectively.
Focus will likely be on growth in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, or OCI, as the company works to expand capacity to meet surging demand for artificial intelligence computing.
OCI growth to exceed the 115%-116% consensus estimate but said margins could become a concern as cloud growth accelerates.
"Faster OCI growth could keep pressuring margins even if revenue beats. The SaaS business isn't growing enough to fully offset this headwind," said the analyst.

at Seeking Alpha, the question is whether Oracle can generate adequate returns on the massive capital investments needed to build AI infrastructure. It sees capital spending and cash flow to remain a weak point even if revenue and cloud growth are strong.

Oracle shares, down about 17% year to date at $162.89, trade at about 20 times expected fiscal 2027 earnings and 14 times fiscal 2028 earnings. Options markets are pricing in a roughly 12% move in either direction following the results, implying a post-earnings range of about $143 to $181.
